title: Captain Walter Dyett and the name Dyack
summary: Welburn asks whether his uncle knew Chicago teacher Walter Dyett; Moore recalls only a name like Dyack, a possible mix-up.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: I see. Did -- does the name Walter Dyett, Captain Walter Dyett ring a bell? It was -- do you thing that your uncle might have known him? He was a music teacher in Chicago, and he taught at the Du Sable High School for many, many years. From a -- this may have been a little after the, the time that you were studying with your uncle, but he studied and taught there from about the '20s into the 1950s.
I believe he played all the instruments, because so many musicians out of Chicago, older and younger musicians, have mentioned his name.
Well, I heard my uncle mention somebody by the name of Dyack.
Oh, a Ukraniam musician. No, this was a black musician.
Oh, oh,oh,oh. Well then it's not the same party. No I don't; I can't recall.
